name: Credit Guarantee Fund Trust for Micro and Small Enterprises (CGTMSE)
teName: సూక్ష్మ మరియు చిన్న సంస్థల కోసం క్రెడిట్ గ్యారెంటీ ఫండ్ ట్రస్ట్ (CGTMSE)
teBrief: కొత్త మరియు ఇప్పటికే ఉన్న సూక్ష్మ, చిన్న సంస్థలకు (MSEలు) ఎటువంటి తాకట్టు లేకుండా టర్మ్ లోన్లు మరియు వర్కింగ్ క్యాపిటల్ రుణాలు అందించడానికి బ్యాంకులు మరియు రుణ సంస్థలకు క్రెడిట్ గ్యారెంటీ కవరేజ్.
ministry: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises
agency: CGTMSE & Small Industries Development Bank of India (SIDBI)
brief: Credit guarantee coverage enabling participating banks and Member Lending Institutions to extend collateral-free term loans and working capital to new and existing Micro and Small Enterprises.
sourceCredit: Source: CGTMSE, Ministry of MSME & SIDBI
briefFull: Credit guarantee coverage enabling participating banks and Member Lending Institutions to extend collateral-free term loans and working capital to new and existing Micro and Small Enterprises.
details:
The Credit Guarantee Fund Trust for Micro and Small Enterprises (CGTMSE) was jointly set up by the Ministry of Micro, Small & Medium Enterprises (MoMSME), Government of India and the Small Industries Development Bank of India (SIDBI) to strengthen institutional credit delivery to the micro and small enterprise sector.

Under the Credit Guarantee Scheme (CGS), eligible new and existing micro and small enterprises can access collateral-free and third-party guarantee-free term loans and working capital facilities through approved Member Lending Institutions (MLIs), including Scheduled Commercial Banks, Regional Rural Banks, Small Finance Banks and select NBFCs.
benefits:
- Enables collateral-free and third-party guarantee-free credit facilities (term loan and/or working capital) from participating Member Lending Institutions.
- Covers both manufacturing and service-sector micro and small enterprises, as well as retail trade and educational/training institutions notified under the scheme.
- Special higher guarantee coverage tiers and concessions apply for micro enterprises, women entrepreneurs, MSEs in aspirational districts and notified priority categories as per prevailing CGTMSE guidelines.
eligibility:
1. New and existing Micro and Small Enterprises (MSEs) as defined under the MSMED Act engaged in eligible manufacturing, service or notified trading activities.
2. Enterprise should hold valid Udyam Registration.
3. Credit facility must be extended by an approved Member Lending Institution (MLI) without collateral security or third-party guarantee on the covered portion.
exclusions:
- Units already categorised as NPA or ineligible under prevailing CGTMSE scheme guidelines.
- Medium and large enterprises outside the Micro & Small Enterprise definition.
howToApply:
1. Prepare a viable business project report and obtain Udyam Registration.
2. Approach a participating Member Lending Institution (Bank / RRB / SFB / approved NBFC) and apply for a business term loan or working capital loan under CGTMSE coverage.
3. The lender appraises the project viability and submits the guarantee coverage request directly on the CGTMSE portal — borrowers do not apply directly to CGTMSE.
documentsRequired:
- Udyam Registration Certificate
- Identity & address proof of promoters (Aadhaar, PAN)
- Business constitution documents (Proprietorship / Partnership Deed / Certificate of Incorporation)
- Detailed Project Report (DPR) and financial projections
- Bank statements, KYC and GST / relevant statutory licences where applicable

faqs.q: Can an entrepreneur apply directly to CGTMSE for a loan?
faqs.a: No. CGTMSE provides guarantee cover to Member Lending Institutions (banks, RRBs, SFBs and approved NBFCs). Entrepreneurs must apply directly to a participating bank/lender for a CGTMSE-backed loan.
faqs.qTe: వ్యాపారవేత్త నేరుగా CGTMSE వద్ద రుణం కోసం దరఖాస్తు చేయవచ్చా?

faqs.q: Is Udyam Registration required for CGTMSE coverage?
faqs.a: Yes, valid Udyam Registration confirming Micro or Small Enterprise status is required by participating Member Lending Institutions.
faqs.qTe: CGTMSE కవరేజ్ కోసం ఉద్యమ్ రిజిస్ట్రేషన్ అవసరమా?
